evidence.title: Australian economy grew 0.4% in the June quarter
supports: June-quarter 2026 real GDP rose 0.4% quarter-on-quarter.
Real GDP was 2.1% higher than the June quarter of 2025.
The ABS characterised growth as subdued and household behaviour as cautious.

evidence.title: Australia economy slows in Q2 but not by enough to fend off another rate hike
supports: Market forecasts were 0.3% quarter-on-quarter and 1.8% year-on-year GDP growth.
Near-term RBA September-hike pricing rose to 57% from 48% after the release.
Australian ten-year yields were also being pushed by renewed US-Iran fighting, higher oil prices and inflation concerns.
evidence.distribution_note: The linked RTÉ page identifies Reuters as its source. WORLD SIGNALS does not treat this syndication page as authority for canonical event timing.

evidence.title: OCR increased by 25 basis points to 2.75%
supports: The Monetary Policy Committee increased the Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.75 percent.
The decision was made by consensus.
The Committee said future policy would depend on the balance of risks to medium-term inflation and did not pre-determine the future OCR path.

evidence.title: New Zealand central bank raises rates by 25 bps, flags gradual tightening path
supports: The article reports that 27 of 31 economists polled by Reuters expected a 25 basis point increase to 2.75 percent.
The headline policy action was therefore widely expected before the decision.
evidence.distribution_note: This evidence record is used only to preserve the reported pre-decision Reuters poll benchmark. It does not establish canonical timing or source authority.

evidence.title: NZ dollar skids as RBNZ flags gradual hikes, Aussie supported
supports: Reuters described the 25 basis point increase to 2.75 percent as expected, while characterising the projected future tightening path as more gradual and limited than markets had priced.
The RBNZ projected the OCR at 2.81 percent by December 2026 and 3.15 percent at the end of 2027, while markets had priced a faster pace and a peak around 3.5 percent.
Two-year swap rates fell 3 basis points to 3.7001 percent after the decision.
The New Zealand dollar fell 0.7 percent to US$0.5893.
Longer-term bond yields were simultaneously being lifted by a global sell-off associated with renewed Gulf fighting, higher oil prices and inflation concerns.
evidence.distribution_note: The Business Recorder page identifies Reuters as the source. WORLD SIGNALS uses it as analytical evidence only and does not treat it as canonical RBNZ provenance.

evidence.title: Quarterly Estimates of Gross Domestic Product for the First Quarter (April-June) of 2026-27
supports: Real GDP grew 7.8 percent year-on-year in Q1 FY2026-27.
The release was posted at 4:00 PM India time on 31 August 2026.

evidence.title: India smashes growth forecasts as investment surges in April-June
supports: Reuters reported Q1 FY2026-27 real GDP growth of 7.8 percent year-on-year against economists' projections of 7.1 percent.
The article identifies high oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty as external risks around the growth outlook.

evidence.title: RBI intervention, dollar flows push Indian rupee to two-month peak
supports: The rupee ended at 94.9500 INR per USD, 0.2 percent stronger than the previous close.
Reuters identified RBI dollar-selling intervention and flow-related dollar supply from foreign banks as the principal immediate drivers.
Reuters also reported that the previous day's strong growth data improved sentiment toward the rupee.
Higher global yields, higher oil prices and renewed US-Iran tensions were simultaneous external headwinds.

evidence.title: BI-Rate Held at 5.75%: Strengthening Stability, Supporting Economic Growth
supports: The 18-19 August 2026 Board of Governors Meeting held BI-Rate at 5.75 percent.
The Deposit Facility rate remained 4.75 percent and the Lending Facility rate 6.50 percent.
BI explicitly cited rupiah stability amid heightened global volatility and the Middle East war, inflation within target and sustainable growth.

evidence.title: Indonesia Central Bank Holds Rates Steady at 5.75%, as Expected
supports: All but one of 28 economists polled by Reuters expected BI to hold the benchmark rate at 5.75 percent.
The decision was the first rate-setting meeting under interim governor Destry Damayanti after the prior governor's resignation.
evidence.distribution_note: The Kontan page identifies Reuters as source. It is analytical evidence only and not canonical event provenance.

evidence.title: MPC Press Release 20 August 2026
supports: The overnight deposit rate remained 19.00 percent and overnight lending rate 20.00 percent.
The main-operation and discount rates remained 19.50 percent.
Monthly headline and core inflation were 0.0 percent in July and below expectations.
CBE retained upside-risk warnings around regional hostilities and fiscal-consolidation pass-through.

evidence.title: HC expects the MPC to hold interest rates at its 20 August meeting
supports: HC Securities expected the CBE MPC to keep interest rates unchanged at its 20 August meeting.
Its rationale included accelerated inflation pressure and higher energy costs alongside a comparatively resilient external position.

evidence.title: Argentina monthly inflation rises in July to 2.1%
supports: July CPI rose 2.1 percent month-on-month versus analyst expectations of 2.0 percent.
June CPI had been 1.9 percent and year-on-year CPI rose to 33.8 percent from 33.5 percent.
Recreation and culture recorded the largest price increases, driven by winter-holiday packages, followed by restaurants and hotels.
